description: CGV-4 Schedule management and CGV-5 Medication management — two sibling management screens with similar add/edit/remove form patterns and no cross-dependency, grouped into one coherent FEAT. Both backends are STUBS (404 until SCH-1 / MED-3); build full UI wired to the documented contract and note the stubs. Depends on FEAT-001. Independent of FEATs 002, 003, 005.
steps: Read context.json and this FEAT file FIRST.

Rebuild app/(caregiver)/schedule.tsx: list via listSchedule() from src/api/schedule. Add/Edit form: title (required), kind (segmented over ScheduleKind: appointment/routine/meal/visit/activity), starts_at (date+time via plain TextInputs with YYYY-MM-DD and HH:MM hints), remind_before_min (numeric), optional person picker (listPeople()), is_quiet_period toggle (send 1|0). RECURRENCE builder from SIMPLE options only: none | daily | weekly (with a weekday multiselect) | monthly (with a day-of-month 1-31). Translate the selection to the backend string: none->null, daily->'daily', weekly->'weekly:MO,WE' (join selected weekday codes), monthly->'monthly:15'. The recurrence string is NEVER free-typed. Create createScheduleItem(input: ScheduleInput), edit updateScheduleItem(id, input), remove deleteScheduleItem(id) with confirm. loading/error/empty states.

Rebuild app/(caregiver)/medications.tsx with two sections. Section (a) Manage meds: list via listMedications(); add/edit form with name (required), dose (required), instructions, optional photo, and one+ times — each time a time_of_day ('HH:MM') + days ('daily' or a weekday multiselect -> 'MO,WE,FR'). Because the client exposes NO standalone medication_times endpoint, send the times inside the create/update payload: build a locally typed payload like `{ ...MedicationInput fields, times: { time_of_day: string; days: string }[] }` and pass it to createMedication/updateMedication (cast if needed), with a code comment that the times wiring awaits MED-3. Edit updateMedication, remove deleteMedication with confirm.

Medications Section (b) Review today's doses: load via todayMedicationLogs() -> MedicationLog[]; show each dose's status (unconfirmed/taken/skipped) and confirmed_by (none/patient/caregiver). The caregiver can confirm or correct a dose via logMedicationStatus(logId, 'taken'|'skipped', 'caregiver').
Implement loading/error (catch instanceof ApiError, show err.message + retry)/empty states on both screens.
Add inline code comments that schedule and medications backends are stubs (routes 404 until SCH-1 / MED-3) and the screens are wired to the documented contract.
acceptance_criteria: Schedule form sets title, kind, start time, reminder lead time and an optional person; recurrence is chosen from simple options and translated to the backend string (never typed); an item can be marked a quiet period.
Schedule items can be added, edited and removed via createScheduleItem/updateScheduleItem/deleteScheduleItem.
A medication can be added with name, dose, instructions, photo and one+ times (time_of_day + days), via createMedication/updateMedication.
Today's doses list shows status (unconfirmed/taken/skipped) and confirmed_by, and the caregiver can confirm or correct via logMedicationStatus(..., 'caregiver').
From mobile/: npx tsc --noEmit prints zero errors and grep -rn 'fetch(' app returns nothing.
findings:
Implemented CGV-4 schedule.tsx and CGV-5 medications.tsx, replacing the Placeholder bodies in place and matching the people.tsx style (useTheme, SafeAreaView+ScrollView, loading/error[instanceof ApiError + retry]/empty states, inline modal Add/Edit form, confirm-before-delete, BigButton, 1|0 SQLite booleans, useCaregiverGate 'Leave caregiver mode').

Schedule (CGV-4): listSchedule() list; form sets title (required), kind (segmented over the 5 ScheduleKind values), starts_at (separate YYYY-MM-DD + HH:MM TextInputs combined to 'DATE TIME' with format validation), remind_before_min (numeric), optional person picker from listPeople() (tolerant: a people failure falls back to no options and does not block the list), and an is_quiet_period toggle sent as 1|0. Recurrence builder uses SIMPLE options only (none|daily|weekly|monthly) and is translated to the backend string in buildRecurrence() — none->null, daily->'daily', weekly->'weekly:MO,WE' (week-ordered selected codes), monthly->'monthly:15'; it is never free-typed and parseRecurrence() reads a stored string back into the controls (unknown values fall back to 'none'). Create/update/delete via createScheduleItem/updateScheduleItem/deleteScheduleItem (delete behind an Alert confirm).

Medications (CGV-5): Section (a) manage meds via listMedications(); form has name (required), dose (required), instructions, optional photo path, and one+ dosing times, each a time_of_day ('HH:MM', validated) + days ('daily' or a week-ordered weekday multiselect -> 'MO,WE,FR'). Because the client exposes NO standalone medication_times endpoint, times ride inside the create/update payload via a locally typed MedicationFormPayload (MedicationInput + times[]), cast to MedicationInput at the create/update boundary with a comment that the times wiring awaits MED-3. Section (b) today's doses via todayMedicationLogs(): each dose shows status (unconfirmed/taken/skipped, color-toned badge) and confirmed_by (none/patient/caregiver); the caregiver confirms/corrects via logMedicationStatus(logId,'taken'|'skipped','caregiver'). The two sections load independently so one stub 404 does not blank the other. Medication name on dose rows is resolved from the loaded meds list (todayMedicationLogs returns MedicationLog without the med name).

Both screens carry inline comments that the schedule and medications backends are stubs (routes 404 until SCH-1 / MED-3) and are wired to the documented contract. All network I/O goes through src/api/* — no raw fetch in app/.

Build gate (from mobile/): `npx tsc --noEmit` CLEAN (zero errors); `grep -rn 'fetch(' app` returns nothing. On-device/Expo Go boot and live calls against the stubbed backend modules were NOT run here.
